text:
maya (Product Designer): Quick design review :figma:  — working on the Playground stream UI. Need consensus on three things: streaming affordance (how new tokens appear), single-action label (Stop vs Interrupt vs Cancel), and whether the prompt library stays fully interactive while a run is active. Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/xyz-playground-stream

kai (Frontend): Sketched a small overlay token pill anchored to the right rail that stays out of the main flow. While streaming it shows token count + tiny indeterminate ring. On completion it expands to show breakdown.

rachel (Engineering): Implementation note: the SSE chunk stream emits partials; interrupt cancels stream token-wise on the server. We don't support resume. So naming must reflect finality (not Pause).

kevin (Accessibility): Agreed — avoid "Pause" if we can't resume. If we land on "Interrupt", button needs aria-label with context: e.g. aria-label="Interrupt generation  Returns partial result" and there should be an aria-live region announcing "Generation interrupted" when action taken.

sara (PM): Customers get confused between "Stop" (looks abrupt) and "Cancel" (might imply nothing saved). "Interrupt" is precise but maybe jargon-y. Alternatives: "Stop generation" vs "Interrupt generation"? Which is clearer?

maya (Product Designer): Preference for "Stop generation" as visible label and secondary tooltip text with the nuance: "Stops generation. Partial response may be returned. Use Regenerate to restart." That keeps button language friendly while documenting behavior.

kai (Frontend): Works for UI. We'll wire button to fire cancel token and render a small toast: "Generation stopped  Partial response returned". Also will debounce token counter updates to 200ms to avoid layout thrash.

rachel (Engineering): For the token pill states: compact (streaming): shows tokens emitted and an estimate of tokens/sec when available; completed: expand with prompt tokens / response tokens / total. Note: interrupt + aggregator fallback may change counts; show microcopy: "Counts may update after stop."

kevin (Accessibility): For token updates, use an aria-live="polite" region that coalesces updates every 300ms so screen readers aren't spammed. Make the pill focusable and provide a visible label for keyboard-only users.

sara (PM): Prompt library: folks want to browse while a generation is running. We should allow browsing but disable "Apply" actions that would affect the active run. Show a tiny banner: "Applies to next generation."

kai (Frontend): Implementation: let library open, keep Apply buttons present but aria-disabled and show tooltip on hover/focus that says "Will apply to next run". Also add a subtle visual treatment so users know it's non-destructive.

maya (Product Designer): In prototypes I'm showing the library as fully browsable with disabled apply CTA and an inline note under the CTA. Also adding a small "switch now" pattern is risky (confusion). Better to keep it conservative.

rachel (Engineering): Edge case: if user selects a new prompt while streaming and then clicks Regenerate immediately after stop, we must ensure the queued prompt is used. We'll track the last selected template in the client state and surface confirmation on regenerate.

sara (PM): Good to call out in docs: "Selecting a prompt during a run will apply to the next generation unless you regenerate after stopping." Might reduce confusion.

kevin (Accessibility): Also confirm keyboard nav: opening prompt library should not trap focus in a way that prevents screen reader users from stopping the generation quickly. Stop button must be reachable via keyboard at all times.

kai (Frontend): On visuals: rather than a full shimmer, propose a short append animation + subtle fade of each incoming chunk. Less flashy, still signals streaming. We'll avoid content layout shift by layering new chunks in an absolutely positioned append area until finalized.

maya (Product Designer): Love that. Add microcopy to token pill tooltip: "Counts are approximate during streaming and may change after stop." And under the stop button: "Stops generation. Partial response may be returned."

sara (PM): Action items: kai to ship prototype with pill + append animation by Tue, kevin to review A11y strings, rachel to validate cancel semantics with infra, maya to update figma copy. deploy-bot: any staging deploys? :hourglass_flowing_sand:

deploy-bot: Scheduled: branch playground/streamflow -> staging on 2025-02-10 03:00 UTC

maya (Product Designer): Thanks team thumbsup If no major a11y blockers we can lock the pattern and iterate on microcopy after user testing.
